items.followUp: What is meant by a scientific name, and what two parts does it contain?

rubric.why: Binomial nomenclature names each organism using two words.
rubric.description: States that each organism is given a two-word scientific name.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the name as having two parts.

rubric.why: The two parts are the genus name followed by the species, or specific, name.
rubric.description: Names the two parts in the correct order.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying genus first and species (specific name) second.

modelAnswer: Binomial nomenclature is the system of naming each organism with two words.
The first word is its genus name and the second word is its species (specific) name.

items.followUp: What are leucoplasts, and where are they commonly found?

rubric.why: Chromoplasts are plastids that contain coloured pigments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying them as plastids containing pigments.

rubric.why: Their pigments give colour to plant parts such as flowers and fruits.
rubric.description: States that chromoplasts give colour to flowers or fruits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the colouring function or a correct example of a plant part they colour.

modelAnswer: Chromoplasts are plastids that contain coloured pigments other than chlorophyll.
They give colour to parts of plants such as flowers and fruits.

items.followUp: Define meiosis and state where it occurs.

rubric.why: Mitosis is a nuclear division that forms two daughter nuclei.
rubric.description: Defines mitosis as nuclear division producing two daughter nuclei.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the division and its two products.

rubric.why: Mitosis occurs in somatic, or body, cells.
rubric.description: States the type of cells in which mitosis occurs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying somatic or body cells.

modelAnswer: Mitosis is the division of a nucleus to form two genetically identical daughter nuclei.
